item.description: The Urban Land Institute (ULI) Central Florida Technical Assistance Panel (TAP) presents its final report on redevelopment and economic development opportunities in Daytona Beach Shores. The report recommends a connected network of four walkable, mixed-use districts: Dunlawton Gateway, Sunglow Pier, a government center and wellness hub, and a north town center and gateway.The panel also recommends improvements to streetscapes, beach access, trails, signage, and connections between destinations. Its suggested economic development tools include targeted property improvements, redevelopment incentives, and public-private partnerships. The report organizes potential actions into near-, mid-, and long-term steps for City consideration.
